title: Few-Shot Prompting for AI-Assisted Summarization of Medical Reports: Optimizing the Transition Between Geriatrics and Outpatient Care.
summary:
In the Geriatric Assessment and Fall Clinic (GISA), older patients undergo comprehensive geriatric assessment and treatment. The resulting outpatient reports contain important information on diagnoses, examination findings, and recommendations for further care. For primary care physicians, promptly identifying this information in routine practice can be challenging due to the complexity and length of the reports.
This research project investigates whether artificial intelligence (AI) can generate concise summaries of anonymized geriatric outpatient reports that are relevant to primary care follow-up. The AI-generated summaries will be compared with expert summaries prepared by physicians.
The quality and practical usefulness of the two versions will be assessed by primary care physicians from Ulm and the surrounding area. Participating primary care physicians will evaluate several pairs of summaries using a questionnaire addressing, among other aspects, comprehensibility, relevance, rapid identification of key information, medical accuracy, expected time savings, and usefulness for primary care. In addition, a subset of participants will take part in short interviews addressing their experiences, perceived benefits, and suggestions for improvement.
The study will use exclusively existing patient data that have been anonymized for the purposes of this project. The study does not interfere with patient treatment. The AI application will be operated locally without an internet connection. The aim of the study is to evaluate the suitability of AI-assisted summaries for more efficient communication between geriatric and primary care.
conditions: Geriatric diseases and geriatric care; evaluation of communication and information transfer between geriatric and primary care.

interventions.name: For each anonymized outpatient report, an AI-generated summary is created using a locally operated Large Language Model (LLM). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Practicing as a primary care physician/general practitioner.
- Working in a primary care practice in or around Ulm, Germany.
- Willingness to participate in the evaluation of anonymized geriatric outpatient reports and their summaries.
- Written informed consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
No specific exclusion criteria.
